title: kernel-prioritizer-prefetcher-hybrid-cohort-notes
content:
Summary:

This is a sketch of a kernel prioritizer + prefetcher that groups inflight requests into small "hybrid cohorts" and steers fused FlashAttention + KV hydration kernels to reduce tail latency when paged KV is active. Goal is to get predictable 95th/99th latency without sacrificing average throughput or too much GPU utilization.

Motivation / background:
- Paged KV means some requests trigger device-side KV hydration (dma) while others hit cached KV. Mixing those in the same launch often increases latency variance: hydration stalls some warps, causing long tail.
- FlashAttention kernels benefit from fusion with KV prefetch/hydration (fewer transfers, better locality), but naive fusion increases worst-case per-request time.
- We need a lightweight runtime-level mechanism to: 1) detect likely-hydration requests, 2) form cohorts that balance hydration vs cached work, 3) pick kernel variants dynamically (fused vs split) and set launch params.

High-level design:
- Kernel prioritizer: small, per-stream scheduler that inspects request metadata (seq_len, prefix-id, kv-tag, recent-hits) and classifies into three buckets: HOT (cached KV likely), WARM (uncertain), COLD (needs hydration). Classification is heuristics + lightweight ML model (see below).

- Hybrid cohorting: collect up to N requests or up to T ms into a cohort. Within cohort, we group by priority and pick a kernel strategy:
  - If cohort HOT ratio >= 0.8 => use fused FlashAttn-fast path with minimal prefetch.
  - If COLD ratio >= 0.25 => pre-warm: schedule small hydration-only DMA baton ahead of compute, then run fused kernel with hydration-aware stalling points.
  - Else => run split pipeline: hydration kernel then FlashAttention compute kernel with small overlap.

- Prefetcher strategy: for cohorts with mixed signals, issue proactive page reads (async memcpy -> device pinned staging) and attach a hydration token to cohort. If hydration finishes early, mark requests HOT for next few steps.

Heuristics & threshold defaults (initial):
- N (max cohort size): 6 requests
- T (max wait): 2 ms (tunable by SLO)
- HOT classifier: prefix-hit count > 2 in last 10 tokens OR last-step KV-hits >= 0.75 probability => HOT
- WARM: confidence between 0.4 and 0.75
- COLD: confidence < 0.4 or explicitly missing pages on GPU
- Proactive DMA size limit: 1 MiB per request for prefetch (cap cohort DMA to 4 MiB)

Lightweight ML classifier (optional phase):
- Model: small two-layer MLP (input shape: [seq_len, model_id_embedding, route_hints, recent_kv_hit_rate]) producing P(hot). Trained offline on recent traces using labels derived from actual page-miss events. Should be quantized to 8-bit and run on CPU core colocated with scheduler (<200us inference target).

Kernel variants we expect to control at runtime:
- flash_fused_light: minimal hydration checks, aggressive tensorcore tiling, low occupancy bias
- flash_fused_guarded: hydration-aware loops, inserts warp-level checks to avoid long stalls (slower but safer)
- hydrate_streamer: pure DMA-driven kernel that pulls KV pages into pre-allocated slab then signals compute
- flash_separate: compute-only kernel assuming KV already resident

Prefetch and fusion micro-protocol:
1) Scheduler groups cohort -> runs classifier -> picks strategy
2) If strategy uses prefetch: issue cudaMemcpyAsync(page_ranges) on dedicated stream with higher priority than compute stream
3) Submit hydrate_streamer with minimal blocksize while allowing concurrent compute on different SMs
4) Barrier: use lightweight event + polling in runtime to avoid global stream synchronization
5) Launch compute kernel variant chosen for cohort

Pseudocode (runtime-level, simplified):

function schedule_request(r):
  tag = classifier.predict(r.meta)
  push_to_pending(tag, r)
  if cohort_ready():
    cohort = build_cohort()
    strategy = pick_strategy(cohort)
    if strategy.prefetch:
      issue_prefetch(cohort.pages)
    submit_kernels(cohort, strategy)

Experiments run so far (hosted testbed: A100 40GB, baseline flashattn v2):
- Microbench: 1x1 batch, seq_len 1024, 12B-ish model config
- Baseline (no cohorting, fused kernels): p95 = 38 ms, p99 = 112 ms, avg = 23 ms, GPU util = 86%
- Split pipeline (hydrate then compute): p95 = 44 ms, p99 = 90 ms, avg = 26 ms, util = 74%
- Hybrid cohorter (N=6, T=2ms, proactive prefetch): p95 = 28 ms, p99 = 62 ms, avg = 21 ms, util = 82%
Notes: hybrid reduced p95 significantly and narrowed p99 vs baseline fused case. The fused baseline had high p99 due to occasional hydration stalls inside fused kernel launch.

Implementation notes / risky bits:
- Need careful stream priority tuning: prefetch on higher-priority copy stream can still be starved if compute saturates PCIe. Test with NVLINK configs too.
- Memory accounting: proactivity can increase device memory pressure on GPUs with tight headroom. Add eviction backpressure signal to scheduler.
- Event polling cost: busy-wait vs sleep tradeoffs — try hybrid polling (spin for X us then sleep).
- Kernel variants maintenance overhead: more kernels -> more testing matrix across model sizes, quant levels.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should classifier be on-device (tiny PPLM on lightweight TensorRT) for <100us inference? Tradeoffs: latency vs accuracy of hot predictions.
- Optimal cohort size under bursty traffic (PLG churn) -- need traces from hosted to simulate.
- Policy for forced flush when cohort waits T ms but has one large COLD request that would blow p99. Consider eviction of that request to lower tier (dedicated slow path).
- How to expose tuning knobs in Console (suggested: cohort_size, max_wait_ms, prefetch_enabled, prefetch_cap_mb, classifier_mode).

Action items (next 3 sprints):
- Sprint 1: implement scheduler skeleton + classifier stub, add two kernel variants (flash_fused_guarded, flash_separate). Owner: Priya.
- Sprint 2: add prefetch streamer + async DMA flow, integrate cohorting logic, run microbench harness. Owner: Luis.
- Sprint 3: optional ML classifier + A/B test in hosted canary, add console knobs. Owner: Jordan.

Appendix - quick debug checklist:
- Reproduce p99 spike: capture timeline with CUPTI + nvprof, verify page async durations
- If p99 correlates with memcpy stalls, instrument stream priorities and measure PCIe saturation
- Use small cohorts (N<=3) in tight loops to validate correctness before scaling

Rough implementation references in codebase:
- serving-runtime/kernels/flash_attn_variants.cu
- serving-runtime/prefetcher/async_hydrate.cc
- tests/microbench/cohorting_experiments.py

End of notes.
